text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Queen Elizabeth II received Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis during his trip to Britain. He also met Prime Minister John Major and discussed the possible terms for Latvia's integration with the EU. On the same day, Guntis Ulmanis visited the editorial office of newspaper The Financial Times.

- Following his lecture in the Royal International Affairs Institute, President Ulmanis announced that the border dispute between Latvia and Russia will be settled early next year, similar to the row between Russia and Estonia.
- No-confidence votes against Welfare Minister Vladimir Makarov and the Minister of Education and Science, Maris Grinblats, failed in parliament.
- German interior ministry experts said that visa regulations with Latvia may be abolished only after the conclusion of a bilateral agreement on the repatriation of illegal immigrants.
- Unibanka and Nomura agreed to start quoting Unibanka's shares in the world's exchanges after a global depository receipt issue in the near future.
- Delegations from Latvia and Poland are meeting in Warsaw to discuss the free trade agreement between Latvia and Poland.
- In response to the president's request, parliament voted for a repeat consideration of the bill on compulsory military service.
- Liquidators of Banka Baltija met in London with Armands Stendzenieks, who owes he bank 18 million lats.
- Since the beginning of privatisation in Latvia, former property owners have recovered more than 10,000 dwelling houses.
